report.source_text: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed the absence of most of the neck, body, and tail of the pancreas (Figs. 1 and 2), and these findings were further confirmed by magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI). However, the pancreatic head was not enlarged (Figs. 3 and 4). Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) revealed the absence of the dorsal pancreatic duct (Fig. 5). There was no evidence of chronic pancreatitis or other visceral malformations.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 23-year-old Chinese woman presented with severe hyperglycemia (fasting plasma glucose 12.29 mmol/L, postprandial 2-hours plasma glucose 22.3 mmol/L, HbA1c 13.4%), very low C-peptide levels, dyslipidemia, and hyperuricemia. Autoimmune markers for diabetes (anti-insulin, anti-islet cell, and antiglutamic acid decarboxylase antibodies) were negative. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) confirmed agenesis of the dorsal pancreas, revealing the absence of most of the neck, body, and tail of the pancreas, and absence of the dorsal pancreatic duct. The patient also exhibited obvious and severe diabetes-related retinal changes on admission. Intensive insulin replacement therapy was initiated, leading to improved blood glucose control.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with severe hyperglycemia and very low C-peptide levels, indicating severe insulin deficiency.
Autoimmune markers for diabetes were negative, ruling out Type 1 diabetes.
MRI confirmed agenesis of the dorsal pancreas, showing absence of most of the neck, body, and tail of the pancreas, and absence of the dorsal pancreatic duct.
Patient had severe diabetes-related retinal changes on admission, suggesting long-standing, uncontrolled diabetes.
Intensive insulin replacement therapy was administered, and blood glucose levels improved.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Negative anti-insulin, anti-islet cell, and antiglutamic acid decarboxylase antibodies.
Low BMI (20.8 kg/m2), very low C-peptide levels, negative family history of diabetes, and severe hyperglycemia at a young age.
Normal amylase and lipase levels, and MRI showed no evidence of chronic pancreatitis (E002).

remaining_uncertainties: Genetic cause of pancreatic agenesis (genetic testing results were not reported).
Long-term clinical course and outcomes beyond initial insulin response.
Full assessment of kidney function (patient refused 24-hour urinary protein analysis).
